hints: Rerooting changes the sum of distances in a predictable way across one edge.
Compute subtree sizes and the total distance sum from an initial root.
Moving root from parent u to child v makes the v-subtree closer by one each and all other nodes farther by one.
analogy: When the root crosses an edge, every node on the child side gets one step closer and every other node one step farther.
example: For a 3-node path rooted at an endpoint, distance sum is 3; at the middle, it is 2.
algorithm: DFS from root 1 to compute subtree sizes and sumDist[1]. For each parent-child edge, sumDist[child]=sumDist[parent]+n-2*subtreeSize[child].
correctness: Exactly subtreeSize nodes reduce their distance by one and n-subtreeSize increase by one, giving the rerooting difference n-2s.
